propositions.text: The Appellant is a citizen of Burundi.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the Appellant) is a citizen of Burundi.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant is a citizen of Burundi.

propositions.text: In 2013, the Appellant joined the Movement for Security and Democracy, later renamed MSD, and became a youth leader in the capital.
propositions.quote: In 2013, the Appellant joined the Movement for Security and Democracy whose name was later changed to Movement for Solidarity and Democracy (MSD) in which he became a youth leader in his neighbourhood of the capital.

propositions.text: He organized and participated in government-banned protests.
propositions.quote: He organized and participated in protests banned by the government.

propositions.text: In June and July 2015, authorities sought him at home and beat his family for his failure to appear after summons.
propositions.quote: In June and July 2015, authorities came looking for him at his home where they beat his family because he had failed to appear after being summoned.

propositions.text: After hiding for three months, he fled to Rwanda, lived there over two years, then came to Canada using a French passport not his own.
propositions.quote: After hiding for three months, he fled to Rwanda where he lived for just over two years before coming to Canada using a French passport which was not his.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant joined MSD in 2013, led protests, was sought by authorities who beat his family, hid, fled to Rwanda, then came to Canada with a French passport.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the asylum claim due to misleading testimony on travel, unsubstantiated safety allegations in Rwanda, and failure to produce APRDH letter.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejected his asylum claim essentially because it found the Appellant's testimony misleading regarding travel from Rwanda to Canada, allegations of not being safe in Rwanda were not substantiated by documentary evidence and that he failed to produce or attempt to produce a letter from the Association Burundaise pour la Protection des Droits Humains et des Personnes Détenues (APRDH).

propositions.text: The RPD noted no written submissions were sent by the Appellant within prescribed delays after notice.
propositions.quote: The RPD also noted that no written submissions were sent by the Appellant within the delays prescribed in a notice sent to him.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claim due to misleading travel testimony, unsubstantiated safety claims, missing APRDH letter, and no timely written submissions.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD erred on notice for written submissions, made irrational credibility findings, misapprehended evidence, and focused on peripheral matters.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits before the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) that the RPD erred regarding notice for accompanying written submissions. It erred in making credibility findings on many aspects that are not internally rational, failed to consider or misapprehended evidence, and further erred by focusing on peripheral matters, being overly microscopic with zeal to find inconsistencies.

propositions.text: He submits four documents as new evidence and requests a hearing before the RAD.
propositions.quote: He submits four documents for consideration as new evidence and requests a hearing before the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues RPD erred on notice, credibility, evidence consideration, focused on peripheral issues, submits new evidence, and requests a hearing.

propositions.text: The determinative issue for the RAD is credibility.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue for the RAD is credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the key issue for the RAD is credibility.

propositions.text: The RAD rejects the new evidence and hearing request.
propositions.quote: I reject the documents submitted as new evidence as well as the request for a hearing before the RAD.

propositions.text: The RPD failed to consider evidence including the Appellant's passport and wrongly inferred credibility from missing APRDH letter when one existed.
propositions.quote: I agree with the Appellant that the RPD failed to consider evidence including his passport, not mentioned in the decision, and by drawing a negative inference regarding his credibility because he produced no letter from the APRDH when there actually was one on record.

propositions.text: The RPD ignored evidence of violence by Burundian militias in Rwanda and focused excessively on travel itinerary, which became peripheral after passport submission.
propositions.quote: As correctly noted by the Appellant, the RPD ignored evidence of violence committed by Burundian militias in Rwanda. It focused on matters such as the travel itinerary which, while initially relevant, became far more peripheral once the Appellant submitted his passport.

propositions.text: The record evidence raises concerns the Appellant could not address at hearing, preventing credibility assessment on core asylum claim.
propositions.quote: However, the evidence which is on the record raises concerns that the Appellant was not given the opportunity to address at the hearing. This precludes me from assessing the credibility of the Appellant with regard to the very core of his asylum claim.

propositions.text: The matter must be sent back to the RPD for redetermination.
propositions.quote: For this reason, I find it necessary to send this matter back to the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects new evidence and hearing request, finds RPD erred on evidence and credibility, and sends matter back to RPD.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed and the matter is sent back to the RPD for redetermination by a different panel.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. I send this matter back to the RPD to be redetermined by a differently constituted panel.

propositions.text: The new evidence presented by the Appellant is rejected.
propositions.quote: NEW EVIDENCE The evidence presented by the Appellant is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal, rejects new evidence, and remands to RPD with a different panel.

propositions.text: Evidence can be accepted only if it arose after the RPD decision, was not reasonably available then, or could not reasonably have been expected to be brought before the RPD.
propositions.quote: According to the law,1 I can only accept evidence that: i. arose after the RPD decision; or ii. was not reasonably available at the time of the decision; or iii. that you could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to bring to the RPD before the decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the legal criteria for accepting new evidence on appeal.

propositions.text: If evidence meets criteria, the court must decide if it is new, credible, and relevant before acceptance.
propositions.quote: If the evidence meets one or more of these requirements, I must decide if the evidence is new, credible and relevant before I can accept it.

paragraphs.summary: The court states it must assess new evidence for novelty, credibility, and relevance before acceptance.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits four documents as new evidence: his affidavit, another affidavit, airport information, and highlighted NDP item 10.2.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits the following documents for consideration as new evidence before the RAD: i. Affidavit of the Appellant sworn January 8, 2020; ii. Affidavit of XXXX XXXX XXXX sworn January 7, 2020; iii. Information on Addis Ababa Bole International Airport ; and iv. Highlighted National Documentation Package (NDP) Item 10.2.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits four documents as new evidence to the RAD.

propositions.text: The Appellant's affidavit was sworn after RPD decision but repeats prior evidence and lacks explanation for unavailability before decision; it is not new.
propositions.quote: Document i., the Affidavit of the Appellant, while sworn after the RPD decision, contains evidence which arose prior to it. In fact, this Affidavit merely repeats or paraphrases the evidence given under oath at the hearing. No explanation is provided as to why any information therein was not reasonably available at the time of the decision or could not reasonably have been expected before the decision in the circumstances. In any case, this evidence is not new as it is already on the record before both the RPD and the RAD in the form of both a recording and a transcript.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's affidavit is not new evidence as it repeats prior testimony and lacks explanation for unavailability.

propositions.text: The second affidavit was sworn after RPD decision but contains prior evidence about the passport and RPD comments; no explanation for unavailability; not new.
propositions.quote: Document ii., the Affidavit of XXXX XXXX XXXX, is dated after the RPD decision. However, the evidence it contains arose prior to the decision. In fact, this Affidavit confirms that the passport of the Appellant was provided during a break at the hearing and that the RPD then commented that the case appeared to be a good one. All this occurred prior to the RPD decision and no explanation is provided as to why any information therein was not reasonably available at the time of the decision or could not reasonably have been expected before the decision in the circumstances. In any case, the evidence pertaining to the passport is not new as this document is already on the record before both the RPD and the RAD. The opinions expressed by the RPD off record, mid-hearing, before all of the evidence had been heard, are not relevant in this context as they do not create, nor are there allegations of, an apprehension of bias against the Appellant, but actually indicate the contrary.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the second affidavit is not new as it contains prior evidence about the passport and RPD comments, with no explanation for unavailability.

propositions.text: The airport information arose before RPD decision, no explanation for unavailability, and adds nothing new to the record.
propositions.quote: Document iii., the Information on Addis Ababa Bole International Airport, regardless of the various dates which appear in it, contains evidence which arose prior to the RPD decision, and no explanation is provided as to why any information therein was not reasonably available at the time of the decision or could not reasonably have been expected before the decision in the circumstances. In any case, this evidence does not appear to add to that already on the record before both the RPD and the RAD and thus is not new.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the airport information is not new evidence as it arose before the RPD decision and adds nothing new.

propositions.text: The highlighted NDP item 10.2 arose before RPD decision and is already on the record, so it is not new.
propositions.quote: Document iv., the Highlighted NDP Item 10.2, arose prior to the RPD decision and is not new as it is already on the record before both the RPD and the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the highlighted NDP item 10.2 is not new evidence as it was before the RPD and on record.

propositions.text: None of the submitted evidence is admitted as new evidence and no hearing can be held before the RAD under section 110(6) IRPA.
propositions.quote: For all these reasons, none of this evidence is admitted as new evidence. Since no new evidence has been admitted, section 110(6) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) does not allow me to hold a hearing before the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects all new evidence and denies a hearing before the RAD under IRPA section 110(6).

propositions.text: The RAD's role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD's role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD decision was correct.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits the RPD erred by failing to consider evidence, notably his passport.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD erred in part, by failing to consider evidence.

propositions.text: The RPD did not mention or analyze the passport or reach a conclusion on identity; the Appellant established identity with his passport.
propositions.quote: Most notably, and by way of example, the RPD enumerates a number of documents in a section of its decision titled "Identity". Nowhere in the decision does the RPD ever mention that a passport was submitted, nor does it ever analyze the identity documents which it did acknowledge, and it never reached a conclusion regarding identity. I find that the Appellant has established his identity with his passport.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues RPD erred by ignoring evidence; the court finds RPD ignored the passport and the Appellant established identity with it.

propositions.text: The RPD extensively examined credibility on itinerary but ignored documents addressing contradictions; credibility on itinerary is mostly peripheral.
propositions.quote: The RPD very extensively examines the credibility of the Appellant's testimony regarding his itinerary, yet ignores some documents submitted by the Appellant in an attempt to address contradictions. In the absence of any finding that the Appellant has not established his identity or that he was not in his country when he was allegedly there, or that he may have returned to his country, I find that his credibility as pertains to his itinerary to be mostly peripheral.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the Appellant that the RPD focused on peripheral issues.
propositions.quote: I therefore agree with the Appellant that the RPD focused on peripheral issues.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD focused on peripheral itinerary credibility issues and ignored documents addressing contradictions.

propositions.text: The Appellant notes the RPD wrongly said violence by Burundian authorities in Rwanda lacked documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: Also, as correctly noted by the Appellant, the RPD affirms in the decision that violence committed by Burundian authorities in Rwanda is not supported by documentary evidence yet ignores the evidence found at item 10.2 of the NDP, which pertains to this question.

propositions.text: The RPD's failure to address evidence of violence in item 10.2 of the NDP is an error, despite possible distinctions between the Appellant and targeted persons.
propositions.quote: While there may be some distinctions to be made between the Appellant and the persons targeted according to this evidence, the failure to address it constitutes an error.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant notes RPD wrongly said violence evidence was lacking; the court finds RPD erred by ignoring item 10.2 evidence.

propositions.text: The RPD wrongly inferred negative credibility because the Appellant did not produce an APRDH letter when one was on record.
propositions.quote: To cite just one more example where the RPD ignored evidence, it specifically made a negative inference regarding the credibility of the Appellant because he produced no letter from the APRDH when there actually was one on record.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD wrongly inferred negative credibility from missing APRDH letter when one existed on record.

propositions.text: Errors in the RPD hearing are determinative of the appeal.
propositions.quote: I find such errors to be determinative of the appeal.

propositions.text: Unable to independently evaluate Appellant's credibility as central questions were not asked at RPD hearing.
propositions.quote: I am unable to independently evaluate the credibility of the Appellant as questions central to determining his credibility were not asked at the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: No questions asked about party name change from 2013 to 2009 per documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: no questions were put to the Appellant as to why he contends in his BOC form that the party that he joined in 2013 was named the Movement for Security and Democracy and later changed its name although the documentary evidence4 indicates that this name change occurred in 2009 when the party was registered.

propositions.text: No questions about why Appellant's card corresponds to specimen ceased in 2009, despite his leadership role in capital.
propositions.quote: He was not asked to comment why the card he was issued corresponds to the specimen which ceased being used in 2009 according to the same documentary evidence, especially since he lived in the capital and had a leadership role there for several years.

propositions.text: No questions about attestation letter showing Appellant living in Burundi in 2017, despite leaving 2 years earlier.
propositions.quote: He was never asked why the attestation letter of the MSD issued in December 2017 indicates that he still lived at an address in Burundi at that time although he left that country 2 years earlier and had no intention of returning there.

propositions.text: Address on letter differs from 2015 address and unlikely from party records; Appellant claims letter issued in Rwanda but address is in Bujumbura.
propositions.quote: The address in question is not identical to that where he lived in 2015 and therefore would not likely come from party records. Although the Appellant contends that this letter was issued in Rwanda, the address printed on the bottom of the letter is one of a neighbourhood in Bujumbura.

propositions.text: Appellant not given chance to explain why assistant to president accepted MSD card with old party name no longer used for 4 years.
propositions.quote: The Appellant was not given the opportunity to explain this nor why this assistant to the president would have been satisfied with the Appellant's MSD card although it was issued on a blank that bearded the old name of the party no longer in use for 4 years at the time that he joined the party.

propositions.text: Appellant not questioned about his party activities or knowledge beyond 2015 protests involving many non-party members.
propositions.quote: The Appellant was not questioned about his activities within the party or his knowledge of the party itself, be it its structure, its program and activities that it held beyond the 2015 protests opposing the 3rd mandate of the president in which several hundred thousand non-party members participated.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds errors in the RPD hearing determinative, noting key credibility questions about the appellant's party involvement were not asked.

propositions.text: These unasked questions are central to Appellant's credibility and were not asked at RPD hearing.
propositions.quote: These questions are central to determining the credibility of the Appellant and were not asked at the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: Section 100(6) IRPA prohibits holding a hearing on matters unrelated to new evidence admitted.
propositions.quote: Section 100(6) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) does not allow me to hold a hearing on matters unrelated to new evidence admitted.

propositions.text: Unable to independently evaluate core asylum claim credibility; case must be returned to RPD for redetermination.
propositions.quote: I am thus unable to independently evaluate the credibility of the very core of the asylum claim and therefore find it necessary to return the case to the RPD to be redetermined.

propositions.text: Unnecessary to address other errors raised by Appellant in memorandum.
propositions.quote: In such circumstances, I find it unnecessary to address other errors raised by the Appellant in the memorandum.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds central credibility questions unasked, cannot hold a hearing on unrelated matters, and returns case to RPD for redetermination.

propositions.text: Appeal is allowed and matter is sent back to RPD for redetermination by a differently constituted panel.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. I send this matter back to the RPD to be redetermined by a differently constituted panel.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal and remands the case to the RPD for redetermination by a different panel.
